evals.prompt: Add Aether streaming chat with persistent history to a Tauri host that already uses providers. Show the required Rust Builder setup, host integration, UI ports, and capability permissions.
evals.expected_output: A feature-consistent integration constructing RunService and ConversationService over the same store, injecting them with Builder::new(logs).runs(...).conversations(...), observability before tauri::Builder, complete KitHost boundaries, createTauriPorts with independent conversations, and matching permissions.
expectations: Constructs the runtime services before injecting them; provider management commands are optional independently of chat
Initializes observability before tauri::Builder
Passes a conversation store when persistent history is requested
Separates compile-time features from Tauri capability permissions
Uses @ouraihub/aether-ui/tauri for ports rather than importing Tauri APIs in components

evals.prompt: Add Skills to an Aether chat application and explain how a changed Skill is handled while a run is being started.
evals.expected_output: A Skills store and UI port are enabled; selected Skills use id plus revision; the backend snapshots the revision, rejects a changed revision, and does not grant tools or silently truncate content.
expectations: Treats Skills as instruction content rather than a permission grant
Preserves id plus revision for selected Skills
Handles revision conflict as an explicit re-confirmation flow
Does not execute imported Skill scripts
Does not silently discard over-budget Skill content

evals.prompt: Review this proposed Aether MCP integration: enable mcp-client, automatically approve every discovered tool, log raw tool arguments for debugging, and let the frontend pass an API key directly to the MCP URL. Identify and correct the security problems.
evals.expected_output: The review rejects automatic approval as a default, raw argument logging, and credentials in URLs or frontend state; it requires backend secret handling, trust and scope checks, typed redacted logging, and host authorization.
expectations: Requires explicit MCP trust and approval policy
Keeps secrets in the backend and out of URLs and DTOs
Rejects raw tool arguments in logs
Preserves the host as the final authorization boundary
Distinguishes cancellation with possible side effects as unknown

evals.prompt: A ChatPanel test invokes real Tauri commands, hand-writes a RunEvent type, and expects RunClient.start to resolve only after the assistant message is complete. Fix the test design according to Aether's contracts.
evals.expected_output: The test injects createFakePorts, imports generated DTO bindings, treats start resolution as acceptance, and asserts event-driven terminal behavior including cancellation.
expectations: Uses createFakePorts instead of real Tauri IPC
Uses generated DTO types instead of duplicate hand-written shapes
Treats RunClient.start resolution as acceptance
Asserts end events for completion and cancellation
Tests observable behavior rather than forwarding implementation
